en: The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Ratnasaṃbhava Dhāraṇī,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Court Dispersing Grandee, Acting Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial,
and Dharma-Transmitting Master, the Subject Shi Hu, by Imperial Decree.

Namo ratnatrayāya, ratnaśrī-saṃdarśana-pratimaṇḍita-vinyasta-tejo-jagad-vaśavara-rāja-tathāgatāya, arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya. Tadyathā: ratne ratne ratnakiṅkiṇi-ratna-pratimaṇḍite ratna-saṃbhavini ratna-pranirātma-nugate svāhā. If there are sentient beings...
Those who uphold and make offerings to the name of this Tathāgata’s dhāraṇī will,
in birth after birth, attain the rank of a wheel-turning monarch,
accomplish the holy life, and possess great supernormal powers.
They shall attain ten kinds of dhāraṇīs and encounter Buddhas and Tathāgatas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, without falsehood;
for koṭis of kalpas, they shall not enter the path of saṃsāra.
One shall not sever the seed of bodhicitta and shall not lose the mind of enlightenment;
all sins will be eternally extinguished, and one will attain the Reward Body (saṃbhogakāya) of the Tathāgata.
If a person recites this for a full seven days, [the result will be achieved].
Such a person shall obtain the pure divine eye.
If a person hears this with their ears and repeatedly recollects it,
that person will certainly attain enlightenment.
The roots of goodness cultivated in past lives will also manifest before one.
If one transmits this to even a single person, all their karma of immediate retribution will be completely extinguished,
and they will forever sever the cycle of saṃsāra.
Such a person will not be harmed by water, fire, thieves, or bandits;
furthermore, their sense faculties will remain unimpaired, no various illnesses will arise, and they will not be possessed by malevolent spirits.
Loved and respected by all, they shall, in future lives, uphold the subtle and wondrous Dharma of the Tathāgata and make offerings to the Buddhas.
If a person, having heard this, rejoices in their heart, prostrates, and offers praise,
that person’s merit will be immeasurable and boundless;
in every successive birth, a sublime fragrance shall emanate from their mouth, extending for one yojana.
The pores of his body are constantly filled with radiance that perpetually illuminates him.
He constantly performs deeds of benefit for the Tathāgata just like Ānanda.
Thus he possesses such inconceivable merit.
The Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on the Ratnasaṃbhava Dhāraṇī.
